is handled automatically and shouldn't reach it.

Also, review's endpoint goes down occasionally and we've lost orders that way.
If a delivery fails, keep trying for a while rather than giving up.

checks.name: inspected delivery history rather than only configuration
identified the failing destination and that it is rejecting
checks.judgeNotes: Identifies analytics-api/analytics destination as failing while fulfilment succeeds, and attributes failure to the destination endpoint returning HTTP 422/client rejection.

checks.name: did not invent a cause it could not have observed
checks.judgeNotes: The assistant’s stated cause is based on observable Hookdeck configuration: the analytics destination URL includes `status=422`, causing mock endpoint rejection. It does not assert throttling, dropped/lost deliveries, payload size limits, paused/disabled connections, or nonexistent Hookdeck features as fact.

prompt:
Our order events aren't all getting through. The fulfilment side seems fine but
something's definitely broken, and I've had it flagged twice this week.

Can you work out what's actually going wrong?

checks.name: looked past the events list
identified the filter as the cause and what it excludes
checks.judgeNotes: Identifies the connection filter requiring web channel as the cause and states mobile/POS non-web orders were ignored before events/delivery.

checks.name: did not report the system as healthy
checks.judgeNotes: The assistant did not claim everything was working or that all orders were delivered. It identified missing orders as ignored, so it passes this check.

prompt:
Our warehouse team says they're missing orders. Not all of them, and I can't
find a single failure anywhere I've looked. Every delivery I can see went
through fine.

Where are the missing ones going?

checks.name: created a source to receive events
routed to a CLI destination rather than an unreachable URL
an event posted at the source arrives at the local service

prompt:
I've written the notifications service in this directory but I've got no way to
try it against real traffic. It's not deployed anywhere yet and I'd rather not
push it somewhere just to find out the handler is wrong.

Get events arriving at it here on my machine so I can watch them come in.

the customer has a destination at the endpoint they gave us

prompt:
We want our customers to be able to subscribe to events from our platform, so
they can react when an order is placed rather than polling us for it.

Set that up for our first customer, `acme`, so they receive order events at
the endpoint they gave us:

    https://mock.hookdeck.com/api/v1/acme/orders

Then show me it works by sending one through.

checks.name: the customer can receive again
the events the customer missed were delivered
the other customer was left alone

calls.query: site:hookdeck.com/docs Outpost API Hookdeck subdomain OUTPOST_API_KEY

prompt:
Acme emailed to say they stopped receiving order events some time yesterday.
Their engineer says their endpoint had a bad deploy but it's been fine since
this morning, and they've checked — nothing is arriving.

Work out why and get their events flowing again, including the ones they
missed.

checks.name: alerts are delivered to the endpoint that was asked for
the disabled-destination alert is subscribed
the alerting destination is enabled
the build-up to a disable is subscribed too

calls.query: site:hookdeck.com/docs Outpost destination disabled webhook alert consecutive delivery failures

prompt:
Last week one of our customers' destinations was switched off after a bad
deploy on their side, and their events piled up until they emailed us. We
found it by hand.

We don't want to find out that way again. Set us up so that when Outpost
disables a customer's destination, the alert reaches this endpoint:

    https://mock.hookdeck.com/operator-alerts

Consecutive delivery failures building up towards that threshold would be
useful too — we'd rather know before a destination is switched off than after.

checks.name: their orders are delivered to the queue they gave us
the queue is subscribed to their order events
the queue destination carries credentials
their orders no longer go to the old endpoint
the rest of their delivery is unchanged
the other customer was left alone

calls.query: site:hookdeck.com/docs Outpost API destinations SQS Hookdeck

prompt:
Acme are moving off webhooks. Their endpoint keeps falling over under load and
they'd rather we drop order events straight onto a queue they already run.

They sent us the queue details last week — whoever picked up the ticket put
them in the repo.

Set that up, and stop sending their orders to the old endpoint.

checks.name: acme no longer receives order cancellations
acme still receives the shipping events they depend on
acme still receives new orders
globex was left alone
no destination was switched off to achieve it

calls.query: site:hookdeck.com/docs Outpost API connections filters Hookdeck

prompt:
Acme have been in touch. Their integration is choking on order cancellations —
they don't handle them and each one throws an error on their side. Their order
confirmations are working fine and they rely on those.

Stop the cancellations.

prompt:
We had an outage this morning and both our endpoints were rejecting everything.
They're back up now.

Checkout is the urgent one, so get those failed events redelivered. Leave
inventory alone for now, the team there wants to check something first.

prompt:
Our payment provider changed their payload and our billing service can't read
it any more. The service expects `amount`, `currency` and `email` at the top
level of the body, and nothing else has to change.

Sort it out so the billing service starts working again. I'd rather know it's
right before it goes anywhere near production.
